title: Nail studio

fields.label: Your style
fields.help: Gel, BIAB, nail art, natural nails... and the look you're known for.

fields.label: Treatments and prices
fields.help: Each treatment with how long it takes and its price; group them (hands, feet, extras) if you like.

fields.label: Favourite shades
fields.help: Shades you love right now, and the brands or kinds (gel, BIAB, classic).

fields.label: Opening hours
fields.help: Each day's hours, and days you're closed.

fields.label: Technicians
fields.help: Who does nails, and what each is best at.

fields.label: Deposit
fields.help: The deposit to hold a booking, if any.

fields.label: Brand colour
fields.help: Optional: your logo or salon colour.

writerNotes: nail: the hero does one nail. Choose the shape, length, a signature shade (its colour and name) and finish that suit the studio, art they would actually do (or none for a clean, minimal studio), the art colour, and a skin tone. Write the six stages for that nail in the studio's voice, each naming its tool or product.
count: minutes the set takes, the coats, how long it lasts, and the four labels; keep them honest for the treatment shown.
menu: the brief's treatments exactly (minutes and prices), grouped into up to four tabs (hands, feet, extras, spa).
shades: four to twelve shades from the brief (or classic shades that fit its style), each with a colour, finish and kind of polish; the names shown for shapes and finishes in the studio's language.
book: opening hours exactly as the brief gives them (null for closed days), technicians (or one entry for the owner) and the deposit (0 if none). The form is a demo: nothing is sent.

hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop; the second part is set in italics); section titles have a second half. theme.accent is the studio's colour, deep enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
